Several men were detained near the British RAF Fairford airbase, which is used by the U.S. Air Force and where B-1B Lancer heavy bombers are stationed, on suspicion of attempting to enter the facility and plant explosives.
Residents of some homes near the base were evacuated, roads were closed, and Army Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) units began checking several vehicles for explosive devices.
Armed police and emergency services were deployed to the base, the perimeter was further reinforced, and footage showing several people being detained near the facility also emerged online.
Amid the incident, RAF Fairford was raised to FPCON Delta, the highest level of security for U.S. military facilities. The level is implemented when an attack has occurred or is considered to be imminent.
RAF Fairford is one of Europe’s key bases for strategic aviation and is regularly used by U.S. strategic bombers.

In a propaganda post, Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Colonel Majed Al-Nazili said Ansar Allah (Houthis) are using Iranian-made air-defense weapons modified into loitering missiles, warning they could pose a serious threat to civilian aircraft over the southern Red Sea. He claimed the weapons were converted with assistance from IRGC experts operating in Yemen and are launched from Ansar Allah-held Hodeidah toward international flight routes.
According to Al-Nazili, the missiles can remain airborne for up to 25 minutes and use heat-seeking technology to home in on heat sources without distinguishing between military and civilian aircraft.
